One-call smoke test of the installed VerteTIME package

Source: R/check.R
vt_check.Rd

Exercises every analytical family and every S3 lifecycle method against the shipped vt_demo compilation and returns a tibble that records which calls succeeded. Use the function as the single command that confirms an installed copy of the package is healthy end-to-end, without depending on any maintainer-private artefact.

Usage

vt_check(verbose = TRUE, plots = TRUE)

Arguments

verbose

Logical, default TRUE. When TRUE, prints a one-screen summary of the call grid to the console as it runs.

plots

Logical, default TRUE. When TRUE, every plot family is exercised (output saved into tempfile()); when FALSE, plot calls are skipped (useful in headless CI without a graphics device).

Value

A tibble with columns family, call, status ("ok"/"error"/"skip"), message, elapsed_s. The result carries an "ok" attribute that is TRUE when every executed row is "ok".

Details

The function loads vt_demo into a private environment, calls one representative function per analytical family, and exercises print, summary and plot on every resulting S3 object. Export functions are exercised against tempfile() paths. The returned tibble lists each call as a row, with the elapsed time and the error message (when applicable).

The function is the canonical smoke test of the installed package: a green tibble proves that data(vt_demo), every metric, every S3 method, every plot family, and the publication subsystem are all callable without touching any maintainer-private folder.

References

Wickham, H., & Bryan, J. (2023). R Packages: Organize, Test, Document, and Share Your Code (2nd ed.). O'Reilly. https://r-pkgs.org.

See also

vt_demo, vt_read(), vertetime, vt_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
v <- vt_check()
attr(v, "ok")
v[v$status != "ok", ]
} # }
